reason: Conversation 2 asked the sensible diagnostic questions (pans, error code, model), explicitly connected the new drawer unit to restricted ventilation with a concrete clearance check, and ended with a correct engineer referral and a clear 'don't dismantle it' boundary. Its weaknesses are a stray 'lift the hob slightly' suggestion, an odd replacement-part model panel, and a final drift toward 'heat sink blocked / replace the faulty part' that under-weights the most likely installation cause and omits the installer/kitchen fitter as the right person to check clearances. Conversation 1 was safe, honest and part-free, but when told the fault began with the drawer fitting it simply said 'nothing changes', never asked about the code, and gave no actionable direction beyond a generic engineer call, so it engaged far less with the homeowner's actual situation.
